notes.8: Question 8 was answered correctly by 42 per cent of the candidates who chose option B . 25 per cent chose option A, 13 per cent chose option C and 20 per cent chose option D . Cheap offers in shops (option B ) are likely to encourage consumers to spend, not to save. The other options would make saving more likely. As income rises it is possible to save more, rich households tend to save more than poorer households and a rise in the rate of interest would encourage people to save as the return on the money saved has increased. It may be that candidates misread the question and thought they were being asked what might increase the level of savings.
notes.11: Question 11 , was answered correctly by 22 per cent of the candidates who chose option B . 34 per cent chose option A , 15 per cent chose option C and 29 per cent chose option D . Minimum and maximum prices and wage rates are often found challenging. It should be remembered that a minimum price or wage rate will not change the market situation if the existing market price or wage rate is already above the minimum.
notes.17: Question 17 was answered correctly by 22 per cent of the candidates who chose option A . 54 per cent chose option B , 11 per cent chose option C and 13 per cent chose option D . Those who chose option B may well have done so because they thought the tax was progressive, as indicated in the third column. Although the amount of the tax levied had increased on the $20 good, the proportion had not changed and so it is not a progressive tax.
notes.23: Question 23 was answered correctly by 46 per cent of the candidates who chose option A . 20 per cent chose option B , 14 per cent chose option C and 20 per cent chose option D . An increase in advertising (option A ) would be an increase in the cost for the industry. The distribution of the responses for the other options might indicate that candidates were guessing the answer.
notes.26: Question 26 was answered correctly by 30 per cent of the candidates who chose option C . 26 per cent chose option A , 10 per cent chose option B and 34 per cent chose option D . In the year, the number of births would have risen by 16 000 and there would have been 8000 deaths so the net change would have been an increase of 8000. However, there was only an increase of 5000. This could be accounted for by 3000 people emigrating (option C ). Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0455 Economics November 2017
